LESSON: LAUNDERING COTTON ITEM

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Laundering cotton item
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Laundering cotton item, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How do laundering cotton items promote hygiene?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Laundering cotton item together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
●Responsibility: The learner takes care of the personal items and hygiene promotion by maintaining cleanliness.

● Unity: The learner shares available resources when laundering white and fast coloured cotton items.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Personal hygiene: The learners practise laundering white and fast coloured items to appreciate the importance of laundry work for personal

hygiene.

Link to other subjects

Science and Technology: The learner uses technology to identify suitable reagents to launder cotton clothes.

Suggested learning resources:

• Cotton clothes-white, fast coloured,

• Detergents, bar soap,

• Clean water

• Drying rack, drying lines, pegs,

• Buckets, basins

• Print and non-print materials,

• Digital devices
